items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: he had put his villa at our disposal with his boy, a native from Biaffra named Benson.

ctx.x: The musicians were mostly young students from different parts of the country and were not very much in the know about jazz, but they loved it & were very cooperative. They had rehearsed in advance standards such as 'Perdido', 'Basin Street Blues', 'St. Louis Blues'. We rehearsed also a couple of Negro Spirituals with the male singing quartet and this was going to be a big success. A couple of the musicians could speak a little English, but I speak French not too badly and as French is the national language spoken…

The U.S. Cultural Center's director was on a trip, but he had put his villa at our disposal with his boy, a native from Biaffra named Benson. The villa was situated in Cocody and was beautiful. We also had a car and a chauffer at our disposal.

We rehearsed the morning and afternoon of the 23rd, also the morning of the 24th and played the first concert that night at the University of Abidjan. It was the rainy season in the Ivory Coast and that day, about 4 p.m., a storm started. Usually, it finished in an hour or two, but that day, we couldn't see the end of it. The concert was open air and we really thought that we wouldn't be able to play. But about 8 p.m., the rain almost stopped, and we left for the university.
